A range of descent options from Middle Peak should be considered: (a) Route 3.83 to the Empress Glacier, then down either to Pudding Rock, or to Empress Hut; (b) traverse to High Peak and descend the Linda Glacier (Route 4.29)—research recent conditions on this route first; or (c) down-climb the East Ridge.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Kaitiaki Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description:
A straightforward climb from Ball Pass, or as part of a traverse from Mt Wakefield to Ball Pass.
The name Kaitiaki (guardian, trustee, or custodian) seeks to recognise a guardianship role of this peak, as a tribute to Aoraki and his brother peaks. For the climbers of ‘Aoraki Bound’, a 20-day cultural and personal journey developed and delivered by Outward Bound and Ngāi Tahu, it is the location from which they can appreciate the majesty of Aoraki Mount Cook without the need to climb the mountain and desecrate his tapu.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Kinsey
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description:
A straightforward climb from either the Hooker or Tasman valley, or as part of a traverse from Mt Wakefield to Ball Pass.
First ascent: Peter Graham, Henrik Sillem, February 1906.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Mabel
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description:
A straightforward climb from either the Hooker or Tasman valley, or as part of a traverse from Mt Wakefield to Ball Pass.
First ascent: James Annan, Malcolm Ross, April 1890.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Rosa
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description:
A straightforward climb from either the Hooker or Tasman valley, or as part of a traverse from Mt Wakefield to Ball Pass.
First ascent: Rosa Moorhouse, Mabel Studholme, 1895.

pitches.description: Can all be climbed easily from the Tasman Valley. Mts Mabel and Rosa provide pleasant climbing up the valley above Husky Flat, but beware of avalanches in spring and early summer. A cut, cairned track exists on the true right of cove stream gorge up to the basin, unmarked on the map. Excellent for descent and a nice alternative to Ball Pass. See topo.

routes.name: From Mt. Mabel
routes.description: A broken, blocky ridge on variable rock in summer. Dropping to the basin is almost always faster in good conditions.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Nazomi
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Originally named Nozomi (Japanese for ‘wish’ or ‘hope’) by Freda du Faur, but it was misread at the time of transcription.

routes.name: North West Face
routes.description: From the upper Noeline Glacier, choose a line up to the central snowfield on the face. Depending on conditions, the route to the snowfield can involve up to two pitches of moderately steep ice and/or rock. From the upper left corner of the snowfield, ascend the couloir (with some rock steps in mid to late summer) which tops out north of the main summit. This is the best descent route from Nazomi but involves careful route finding. The steep steps between smaller snowfields can usually be abseiled with only one 50m rope.
routes.ascent: Freda Du Faur, Alex Graham, Peter Graham, March 1912

routes.name: Du Faur Ridge
routes.description: The southern wall of the Noeline Glacier can be gained at various points, and although the upper portion has been climbed often, the ridge does not appear to have been climbed in its entirety. Excellent rock buttresses are found on the lower ridge.

routes.name: Tim Jefferson Memorial Route
routes.description: The stunning red slab clearly visible from the top of Pudding Rock (old Gardiner Hut site), on the western end of the west ridge of Pt 2560m. Climb the north side of the buttress using the obvious left facing corner for three pitches, turning two large roofs on the left. Move onto the broken slabs of the west face through an overhanging ‘V’ slot on the north-west ridge (crux). Easy scrambling along the ridge then leads to a point above a large snow slope leading down the north side, to the Noeline Glacier descent route. Plenty of scope for other climbs on the first slab.

routes.name: White Vervoorn Buttress
routes.description:
If you can’t get onto Pudding Rock but have favourable weather and time, this would be a very nice consolation climb. Gain the buttress from the Hooker Glacier below the Hooker icefall. Involves moderately hard climbing on excellent rock (grade 13–15).
‘I’d say the starting altitude would be about 1500m and the rope work continues to about 1900m, after which it becomes a walk up snow and maybe a bit of ice here and there. Dave and I went no further up than circa. 2500m, where the ridge line levels off.’ – Aat Vervoorn

routes.name: MacInnes Ridge
routes.description:
A sustained classic with a better cheval than Malte Brun’s West Ridge. Some parties have taken a long time on this climb, so don’t underestimate it. Starting from the lower Hooker Glacier beside the stream from the Mona Glacier, climb the first buttress (the only continuous loose rock of the climb), then onto the second buttress of good rock (with a 20m cheval) and up to the ‘Gnome’, from where a short descent leads onto a small glacier below the final wall. An escape route above Pt 2560m exists to the left. Otherwise, continue straight up variable rock to the summit ridge. This section can often be iced up.
Lincoln Hall and Tim McCartney-Snape made a superb link up of MacInnes Ridge and Aoraki South Ridge in the summer of 1977-78.

places.name: Gledhill Buttress
places.access: Access via the Noeline Glacier has its fair collection of objective hazards in the form of ice cliffs, rock fall, and glacial manoeuvres.
places.description: The Gledhill Buttress is probably the best rock climbing real estate in the Hooker valley.

routes.name: Castle McDermott
routes.description:
Start up the toe of the Buttress and move left into the
corner after 20m. Continue up the corner then through the middle of the upper slabs to traverse back right to cross the roof line in the upper wall. The party mistook this for the Gledhill Buttress.

routes.name: Gledhill Buttress
routes.description: The most popular option (used on the first ascent, 101i on topo) starts up the obvious corner. Continue up the corner for about four pitches, then choose a route up the upper slabs, weaving back and forth as necessary to bypass overhangs (crux 16-17 depending on routefinding). There are many variations on the upper third of the buttress.

routes.name: Gledhill Buttress Direct
routes.description: A direct variation to Gledhill Buttress heads straight up the prow on compact rock (101ii on topo), easing back for the upper portion.

routes.name: Terminator
routes.description: A staunch route on excellent rock. Climb the first two pitches of the Gledhill Direct, then after the climbing eases slightly head out right on a hanging ramp (great fun) to climb through the prominent overhang right of the prow. Continue straight up through another overhang to re-join the Direct where it eases back.

routes.name: Variant
routes.description: Start 70m right of the Gledhill Buttress near a waterfall. Climb face to overhang, then up groove and steep gully, and follow a rib to the top. Excellent rock. Possibly involves the Tom and Bill Route.

routes.name: Tom and Bill
routes.description: Climbs the prow of the next buttress to the right of the main Gledhill Buttress, with ledges halfway. Limited protection. The final 200m before the summit eases back.

pitches.description: Follows the major ice line to the left of Runts in Paradise. Ben started out by heading up frozen snow from the schrund and then up steeper waterfall ice in a gully on the right. The first 15-metre high step of over 85-degree ice was the crux of the 450-metre face, which alternated between ‘short ice steps’ and snow, leading up to steeper mixed terrain before hitting the ridgeline. Another 150 metres along the ridgeline allowed access to the summit
Gullies left of the Faintly French Route, with a snow slope to start. This route climbs ice to the left of the left rib and takes a left-hand  gully at half height.

routes.name: No country for old men
routes.description:
Seven 60m pitches, starts up snow slopes as for Runts in Paradise but
continues up closer to the left rib (Faintly French) when Runts heads left
and up.
routes.ascent: Felix Landman and Llewellyn Murdoch, 18 November 2011

pitches.description: Climb the left rib, rock scrambling changing to steep climbing on an arête (crux 15) followed by easier broken rock 200m below the summit.
The obvious central couloir between the two major buttresses.

routes.name: Cormack-Wilson Rib

pitches.description: Up the middle rib which steepens in the middle before reaching a shelf below the final 150m of poor rock.

routes.ascent: H W Cormack, L W Wilson, Dec 1936.

routes.name: Andy's route
routes.description:
Ice line immediately R of Cormack -Wilson rib and left of Slightly Scottish.
Was ascended accidentally being mistaken for the line of Slightly Scottish
due to that having been wrongly marked in earlier Guide books.. Immediately
got a second ascent by Sam Bossard and Paula MacFarlane

routes.name: Slightly Scottish

pitches.description: "The" line on the face to date. An ice climb up the couloir to right of Cormack-Wilson Rib. Sustained climbing through middle section with vertical and overhanging ice encountered. When first climbed there was pronounced rockfall on the first two piches as  the bottleneck collects all debris between Cormack-Wilson rib and  TTSB.  Objective danger should lessen rapidly     on subsequent pitches. 450/500m depending on the collection/debris cone at the base.

routes.description:
An ice climb up the couloir to right of Cormack-Wilson Rib. Where the couloir
cuts right to the South Ridge move left and up (crux) to reach the shelf,
then out onto the upper South Ridge.
17 x 40m pitches. This is a steep climb and further R than Andys route. They
share the same finish
routes.ascent: Murray Ball, Bryan McArthur, Zane Williams, Jan 1980.

routes.name: The Turkey Strikes Back (Right Rib)

pitches.description: Third buttress right of the MacInness R. A rotten rock start leads to climbing on sound compact rock with sustained difficulties

routes.ascent: Roddy McKenzie, Craig Nottle, Graeme Saunders, Jan 1982.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: The start from the head of the Mona Glacier Névé is steep and has been avoided by using couloirs on the west to emerge where the ridge flattens. A prominent tower 200m below the summit is turned on the east. The rock is variable.

places.name: East Face
places.description: From the junction of the Ball and Caroline Glaciers, ascend a rib to gain the prominent shelf that runs below Nazomi and verges the Caroline Face. A number of routes exist from the shelf onto the crest of the Aoraki / Mt Cook Range:

routes.name: Gillies-Rodda

pitches.description: From the Ball Glacier gain the prominent shelf that runs below Nazomi and verges the Caroline Face by climbing 650m up a rib that starts from the Ball-Caroline glaciers junction.

routes.description: To the base of the South Ridge, then up the ridge.

routes.name: Plato Goes to Japan
routes.description: A prominent snow arête leading to halfway up the South Ridge.

routes.name: Northern Arête

pitches.description: A snow arête leading to the north summit.

routes.ascent: D C Ball, David Herron, Phil Houghton, Fred Page, Richard Tornquist, Jan 1959

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Turner Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Proud Peak is essentially an outlier of Turner Peak and it seems odd that they are named separately. Here, and in the Aoraki Tai Poutini guide (2018) they are treated as one peak.

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: Straightforward rock scrambling and snow slopes. Climbing on the northwest face is also possible.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: An enjoyable rock climb from the scree slope above the Hooker Glacier. The upper section of the ridge can also be accessed from the lower Mona Glacier.
routes.ascent: G Carr, K E Johnson, January 1965

routes.name: South Face
routes.description: Several routes about 250m long, which are easily accessible from Ball Pass. Most routes involve a combination of steep snow and up to WI2+ ice. Harder variants with WI3+ steps at the start are possible. Generally steep at first then onto 60 degree neve ramps with some small steps, 70-80 degrees max. Climb when conditions are fat, rock gear would be nix. Named Névé Névé Land by Jaz Morris in 2013 on what he thought was the first ascent.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: A more interesting option than Route 4.02, but also more time-consuming.

routes.name: East Flank
routes.description: From Ball Pass, or the snowfield below and east of the pass, pick a line up snow and rock slopes to the summit. A number of variations are possible. Refer to Chapter 3 for routes on the other aspects of Turner.

routes.name: From Cassel Flat
routes.description: Start from the Karangarua River opposite the Tui Creek junction to gain the west ridge, which is followed up through thick scrub then along an easy ridge to the summit.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: Traverse from The Clue. An excellent viewpoint. Originally named Liberty Cap by A P Harper due to its appearance from the upper Douglas valley.

routes.name: North Face
routes.description: From the lower end of the Douglas River flats beneath The Pommel (BX15 525 573), start climbing up the true right side of the creek which drains a large shelf below Red Deer Col. Where this stream forks, take the true left fork, and then soon afterwards climb out onto the true left bank, sidle across to the right (west) and angle up onto a spur. This takes you to a tussock bench on the lower part of the large shelf. From 1150m on the shelf, head left using interconnecting tussock ledges, cross the major waterfall at about 1350m, and zig-zag up just right of the left edge of the face ‘basically following ledges with the odd tricky metre or three’.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: Gain Red Deer Col from either the Douglas or Karangarua valleys – see Route 15K on the Karangarua River page. A straightforward traverse from Red Deer Col.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: The Abbott
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Abbey Pass and The Abbott at the head of Pinnacle Stream, November 2016

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: From Jollie Peak, a long scramble, exposed in places, leads to the summit.

routes.name: From Abbey Pass
routes.description: An enjoyable scramble from Abbey Pass. A terrific viewpoint. Also marked on topo as route 6.70.
routes.ascent: C S Brocket, N D Dench, N Feierabend, J Harris, January 1953

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: The Acolyte
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: First climbed by Peter Graham, Miss Joachim, J Stout in March 1917 (route unknown) and in winter by John Herbison, Faye Kerr, June 1979 (route unknown).

routes.name: Botanical Spur
routes.description: A scrub bash leading to a scenic scramble up the north-west ridge.

routes.name: Irish Creek Route
routes.description: Boulder hop up the creek to gain either the north-west ridge or south-west ridge, which provide straightforward scrambles to the summit.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: The Ant-hill
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: The Ant-hill, Armadillo Saddle and Conrad from the top of the Harper Glacier, December 2016

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison Glacier, head up the stream draining the Harper Glacier on the true left. The head of this stream is surrounded by bluffs, but there is a sloping, bouldery shelf running through them that begins at 1800m, grid ref BX16 915 763. This leads up to 2000m at about grid ref BX16 918 762. Gain the col south of Pt 2429m and ascend the straightforward rock ridge.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description:
From Armadillo Saddle, climb scree and snow slopes to the summit.
A good ski touring option from The Ant-hill heads north to the saddle south of spot height 2429m. Ski around the spur of this point on its eastern side to gain the glacier basin east of Mt Richmond. Then ascend towards Mt Acland and gain access to the Aida Glacier via the small notch at about 2400m.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: The Armchair
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: The knob above the corner where the Murchison River joins the Tasman valley.

routes.name: Various Routes
routes.description: Hardly ever climbed, but probably an interesting outing.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: Gain the saddle east of the peak from either the Aida or Harper Glaciers, and then up the short ridge to the summit.
routes.ascent: S Drake, W F Crawshaw, David Hall, January 1947

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Jollie Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Southern Liebig Range, Jollie Pk to Mt Biretta, March 2016

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: Pick a line from the Murchison valley floor to the basins north east of the peak, then climb up to the range crest and scramble to the summit. Pt 2454 (the other ‘Jollie Peak’) is also easy from here.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Monastery Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Southern Liebig Range, Jollie Pk to Mt Biretta, March 2016

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison riverbed, head up grass and scree slopes to a basin north-east of the peak, then pick a line onto the ridge and up to the summit.
routes.ascent: Peter Graham, A Humphries, R B Seager, March 1918

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Acland
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Liebig Range peaks above Aida Glacier, September 2013

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: Traverse from the col between Acland and Sydney King, with a couple of short steep rock slabs.

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: From the Aida Glacier, climb snow slopes to high on the south ridge.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: From the Aida Glacier, climb to the col between Mt Richmond and Mt Acland, then follow the ridge to the summit.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Biretta
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: A biretta is a type of square cap, worn by Catholic clergy.

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: From the lower Murchison valley, this is a scramble from the high basin west of Monastery Peak.
routes.ascent: Tom Fyfe, Malcolm Ross, Samuel Turner, December 1905

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Conrad
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Liebig Range from Mt Richmond to Godley Pass, March 2016

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description:
From slopes west of Armadillo Saddle, either (i) traverse below the ridge crest on scree and snow slopes, gaining access to the ridge roughly 200m from the summit or alternatively (ii) stay on the crest all the way from Armadillo Saddle. Two rock steps near the summit offer good quality climbing.
First ascent of the full ridge from Armadillo Saddle is unknown.
routes.ascent: K Wade, I Dainis, January 1965 (descended final section of ridge)

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: The basin below Conrad’s west face can be reached directly from the Murchison via a straightforward moraine wall (2012), or via a sidle from Armadillo Saddle at around 1800m to 2100m. The face involves 300m of pleasant rock. The first ascent party descended the South Ridge.
routes.ascent: Shelley Hersey, Paul Hersey, Jamie Vinton-Boot, January 2012

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: From Godley Pass, scramble up the rock ridge over the 2400m peak to the summit, or access the ridge from the basin below the west face. This is the easiest descent route.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: A great line. The climbing consists of technical rock scrambling with sustained exposure. The rock quality is unknown. The South Ridge probably offers the best descent option.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Hutton
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Mt Hutton is a large mountain that can be seen from practically the full length of the Cass valley, and demands more attention from climbers than it has so far received.

routes.name: South West Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison, head up beside the waterfall opposite the Baker Glacier, over grass and scree to the hanging valley west of the peak. Alternatively, if the moraine wall dictates, traverse into this valley from further north or south. Continue to the crest of the ridge using the rock rib between Pt 2554m and 2563m col, and then follow the ridge to the summit, traversing snow domes along the way.

routes.name: Full South West Ridge
routes.description:
Gain Rutherford Pass and then continue almost 3km along the ridge to the summit. A great outing, probably best climbed when snow-covered. It would make a great ski tour.
May be best climbed from the Cass, which was first completed by R Boot, J N Hamilton and G A Walker in October 1951.
routes.ascent: Ian Powell and Hutt Valley Tramping Club party, 1944

routes.name: Moonshadow
routes.description: Climb the centre of the rock wall on the south face above the Faraday Glacier.
routes.ascent: Alastair McDowell, Caleb Jennings, Rose Pearson, August 2018

routes.name: East Face
routes.description: Climbed from the Huxley Glacier up moderate snow slopes with some short rock steps. The first ascent party descended the north side of Mt Hutton, then climbed over the range south of Pt 2778m and down Rankin Ridge.
routes.ascent: Gerry Essenberg, Dave McLean, Rob Moffat, early 1990s

routes.name: Rankin Ridge
routes.description: From Rankin Pass, scramble up the rock ridge to Pt 2373m, then ascend crevassed snow slopes to the range south of Pt 2778m.
routes.ascent: Gerry Essenberg, Dave McLean, Rob Moffat, early 1990s (descended)

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison Glacier, scramble up moraine, grass, and scree to the snowfield north of the peak, and then climb a snow gully to the Hutton – Ronald Adair Col. Traverse south-west over the low peak to the high peak.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Kenneth
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Liebig Range, Mt Olaf to Mt Hutton, March 2016

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison Glacier, climb up into basin beneath Mt Ronald Adair, then climb rock and scree (and snow, depending on the season) to gain the Olaf – Kenneth Col. Now climb the north ridge on poor rock.
routes.ascent: Alf Brustad, Kenneth Grinling, Adair Algie, Ronald Algie, January 1927

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: From the head of the north branch of the Rankin Stream climb a narrow snow gut to gain the ridge. Once on the crest, continue over loose rock to final snow slopes and the summit.
routes.ascent: A Baird, B S Charman, W E Limbrick, January 1959

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Lucia
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Mt Lucia is an alluring rock peak when viewed from the Cass.

routes.name: North West Ridge
routes.description:
From Kehua Pass, a rock scramble along the ridge via Pt 2523m leads to the summit. It is also possible to climb up scree and snow slopes into a couloir that leads to about halfway along the ridge.
C S Brockett, N D Dench, N Feierabend and SJ Harris reached Pt 2523m in January 1953. The first full ascent was from the Murchison via Mt Tamaki.
routes.ascent: Alex Parton, Nick von Tunzelmann, December 1963

routes.name: South East Ridge
routes.description: Ascends from the confluence of the Ailsa and Cass valleys. A long, exposed rock scramble, which could have occasional snow arêtes depending on the season.
routes.ascent: J T Cruse, N J Mitchell, W Nixon, December 1956

routes.name: North Face
routes.description: From the upper Cass, ascend scree slopes then a snow couloir to gain the ridge east of Pt 2523m. Essentially an access route to the upper north-west ridge.
routes.ascent: JT Cruse, NJ Mitchell, W Nixon, December 1956 (descended)

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Olaf
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Liebig Range, Mt Olaf to Mt Hutton, March 2016

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: From Godley Pass. Consists of scrambling on poor rock for quite a long way.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison Glacier, climb up into the basin beneath Mt Ronald Adair, then climb rock and scree (and snow, depending on the season) to gain the Olaf – Kenneth Col. From the col, climb the ridge of poor rock to the summit.
routes.ascent: Adair Algie, Ronald Algie, Alf Brustad, Kenneth Grinling, January 1927

routes.name: North West Ridge
routes.description: An easy climb along a snow ridge from Classen Saddle.
routes.ascent: Jack Stenhouse, Geoff Harrow, Rosemary Packer, Lyndsay Alston, Don Young, Rodney Hamilton, August 1956

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description:
From the Aida Glacier, climb the spur leading towards Mt Sydney King to gain the col between Mts Phyllis and Sydney King, then up the ridge to the summit.
First ascent unknown, but the col between the Joie de Vivre and Aida Glaciers was first crossed by Archie Scott, Russell Fraser and Alf Brustad in January 1933.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Richmond
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Liebig Range peaks above Aida Glacier, September 2013

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: A straightforward snow and rock scramble.

routes.name: North West Face
routes.description: From the Aida Glacier, climb rock bands and snow slopes to the summit.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: Gain the saddle east of Coopers Mate from either the Aida or Harper Glaciers, and then climb rock slabs to the summit.

routes.name: South West Face
routes.description: Appears to comprise moderately steep snow and mixed climbing. The first ascentionists accessed the Harper Glacier from the Aida Glacier, crossing over the saddle east of Coopers Mate.
routes.ascent: C Morris, W Provan, M Clark, December 1980

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Ronald Adair
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Liebig Range, Mt Olaf to Mt Hutton, March 2016

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: From the summit of Mt Kenneth follow the loose rock ridge with the odd snow patch to the summit.
routes.ascent: Alf Brustad, Kenneth Grinling, Adair Algie, Ronald Algie, January 1927

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: From the Murchison Glacier, scramble up moraine, grass, and scree to the snowfield north of the peak, and then climb a snow gully to the Hutton – Ronald Adair Col. From the col, a fairly long, undulating scramble over loose rock leads to the summit.

routes.name: East Face
routes.description: Takes a line straight up the middle of the face, direct to the summit. Described by the first ascentionists as ‘straightforward snow and ice slopes with a couple of rock sections’.
routes.ascent: Rob Moffat, Steve Tulley, Gerry Essenberg, July 1993

routes.name: East Ridge and South Face
routes.description: From the Aida Glacier, climb the spur leading towards Mt Sydney King then pick a line to the summit. A great ski tour in spring.
routes.ascent: Otto Frind, Conrad Kain, March 1914 (traversed from Acland)

routes.name: Joie de Vivre Buttress
routes.description:
From the upper Joie de Vivre Glacier, climb the rock buttress directly to the summit.
The feasibility of direct access from the Classen to the Joie de Vivre is unknown. It may be easier to either start further down valley, using slopes below the north ridge of Mt Sydney King, or drop onto the upper Joie de Vivre Glacier from near the summit of Phyllis.
A NZMGA guides course added a number of routes on this buttress in March 1991.
routes.ascent: R Coombs, D Launder, G Vickers, December 1968

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Mt Tamaki
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: An excellent viewpoint. From the 1910s to 1950s this peak was often incorrectly referred to as Mt Lucia.

routes.name: South East Ridge
routes.description: A straightforward rock scramble from Kehua Pass.
routes.ascent: Alex Parton, Nick von Tunzelmann, December 1963 (descended)

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: From Rutherford Pass, traverse the crest of the Liebig Range over Pt 2382m.

routes.name: From the Murchison
routes.description: A straightforward rock scramble from Rutherford Pass or more directly from the floor of the Murchison valley.

routes.name: South West Ridge
routes.description: Ascend snow slopes to the Liebig Range south-west of the summit, then scramble to the top.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: The Nuns Veil
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: The Nuns Veil and Gorilla Stream, November 2012

routes.name: Nuns Veil Glacier Route
routes.description: A popular climb, and for good reason. The route is not too technical and the summit offers a glorious viewpoint. However, there’s an exposed traverse near the top of the glacier that takes a lot of people by surprise. Gorilla Stream was formerly known as 'Griller Stream.' You’ll understand why if you’re there on a hot day. From upper Gorilla Stream, ascend the Nuns Veil Glacier to the summit. This mostly involves straightforward snow slopes, but around 2600m there’s a traverse over a big drop down towards the Tasman valley, which can often be icy. It’s not too steep, but if you’ve got people that aren’t too confident on sustained snow slopes then you’ll want a rope and some snow stakes. The effort is well worth the view. Descent is by the same route.
routes.ascent: Peter Graham, Mick Collett, Dr Mackay, 1905

routes.name: Nuns Veil Glacier Variation
routes.description: The Nuns Veil Glacier Route has been climbed from Pinnacle Stream, via the col north of Pt 2416m.
routes.ascent: C S Brockett, S J Harris, N D Dench, January 1953

places.name: East Face
places.description: This face is big, and not often viewed. Unless you’ve got an exceptional memory, take a photo of it with you on your climb.

routes.name: Curb Your Enthusiasm
routes.description: The leftmost of the three prominent buttresses. Begins with two pitches of grade 17 climbing on good rock, then most of the remaining 15 pitches are on rock of “less than good quality” with little protection and poor belays. The crux is the top pitch of the central rock step. The first ascent team descended the Nuns Veil Glacier after a lesson in navigation.

routes.name: The Far Side
routes.description: A visionary line that takes the impressive central buttress of the east face and requires commitment. There is plenty of room for variations. The first ascentionists reported 700m of quality rock (16 pitches) with a crux of 16. A subsequent party has described the route as sustained grade 16 with crux pitches of 18, reporting “variable rock” and “a few moments of brilliance”. A party that completed a variation finish to the left of the original line may have experienced suboptimal routefinding due to climbing the last five pitches in the dark.

routes.name: North East Buttress
routes.description: A great looking feature. The buttress is broad at the base with a number of possible routes, although higher up it narrows to a defined crest. 17 pitches. The rock is reportedly “pretty good”.

places.name: West Face
places.description: The Nuns Veil from the west, January 2013

routes.name: Turners Couloir
routes.description: From the true left bank of the lower Murchison River in the Tasman valley, ascend an unnamed creek to the prominent couloir leading up between Nuns Veil and Mt Biretta. From the top of couloir climb a rock ridge to the summit.

routes.name: Unveiled
routes.description: Takes the central buttress on the west face. Head up the groove on the left hand side of the face, continue past two rock shelves (the top one may be snow covered), then tend left into a gully leading to the top. The route involves 900m of climbing, involving compact pink slabs, chimneys, and scrambling.

routes.name: After Thought
routes.description:
Super rock quality except for one loose section in middle of face. Head up centre buttress to the impressive head wall. 10 pitches. One pitch with great hand jams.
Climbs to Pt 2520m south of Nuns Veil.
Descend to the south on the eastern side of ridge then to the west down the col.

routes.name: Five O’Clock Shadow
routes.description: Head up the face trending slightly right to summit on Pt 2285.  Descend the gully north of the summit. Great rock quality.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Matenga Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: South face of Matenga Peak, December 2017

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: Easiest access and probable first ascent line.

routes.name: Mixed Blood
routes.description: Four pitches up the prominent corner system on the left side of the face. The first pitch is spicy, with some marginal gear during the first ascent. Difficulty is highly dependent on the amount of ice present. To descend, either abseil the route, continue to the summit and descend the west ridge, or descend the east ridge.

routes.name: Cleavage
routes.description: Straight up a deep couloir in the middle of the face, in places only a couple of metres wide. Sections of water ice interspersed with snow. Three pitches. Second pitch is the crux.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Beatrice Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Beatrice and Dilemma from the summit of Aoraki

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: Traverse from Lean over Edith and Raureka.
routes.ascent: Hugh Chambers, Peter Graham, Dorothy Holdsworth, January 1914

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: From Baker Saddle, traverse snow slopes on the Hooker side of the range until it is possible to climb to the ridge crest either directly to the summit or slightly south. It is also possible to gain the Main Divide north of the summit, but obstacles on the ridge may force you off again in places.

pitches.description: From the névé of the Explorer Glacier climb mixed ground (with rotten rock) to just south of the summit.

routes.name: Main Divide Route

pitches.description: The Divide ridge from Glacier Peak is a pinnacled, enjoyable climb. Also refer to Upper Tasman Glacier Section.

routes.ascent: Harold Porter, Vic Williams, Dec 1930 (from the east).

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Brodrick Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Mt Brodrick, the upper Murchison Glacier and Mt Mannering, December 2011

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: From Whymper Saddle, follow the Main Divide, firstly on snow then rock to the Low Peak (about 2610m), and then continue to the summit.
routes.ascent: D W Beatty, P A L Fraser, A W McNaught, J V McNulty, January 1955 (reached the low peak)

routes.name: South West Rib
routes.description: Described as ‘the vague feature on the left side of the peak when seen from Murchison Hut.’ Leads to within 100m of the summit.

routes.name: Loves Last
routes.description: Climbs the central gully of the south-east face, finishing just right of the summit. When first climbed, the gully consisted of snow/ice low down and mixed climbing higher up.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: Climb the ridge from Classen Saddle, which leads to snow slopes to arrive high on the Main Divide north of the summit, and then continue to the summit. An enjoyable route in spring. This or the North East Ridge usually offer the best descent from Brodrick.

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: From Classen Saddle, traverse to the vicinity of Whataroa Saddle, then up snow or rock slopes east of the divide to reach the ridge southwest of Pt 2442, and then traverse the Main Divide to the summit.

pitches.description: Drop into the névé from a point west of Whataroa Saddle. Climb the prominent rib on the face, gaining the north ridge, then continue to the summit.

Six pitches of excellent red rock. Start just left of the major left facing corner and finish 100m below, and to the south of the summit (crux 15/16). The slabs can be seen from the Main Divide between Hochstetter Dome and Aylmer. Climbed from the upper Whymper (see the back cover photo of the Mt Cook guidebook).

routes.name: North Buttress

pitches.description: Climb the buttress at the head of the true right branch of the Whymper Glacier.

routes.ascent: Dave McNulty, Ray Button and four NZMGA course participants, Mar 1986

pitches.description:
From Whataroa Saddle follow the rock and snow ridge of the Main Divide or snow slopes to
the south-east.

routes.name: South West Ridge
routes.description: Travel as per the Main Divide route on The Footstool as far as the crest of the Divide, then an easy ridge to the summit.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: Via the rock ridge between the Eugenie and Hayter Glaciers, then a rib right of centre on the east face. Either gain the ridge from Sefton Bivvy by crossing the east ridge of The Footstool and the Eugenie Glacier, or climb all the way from the valley floor (a true adventure). The upper part of the climb is a bad area for slab avalanches early in the summer.
routes.ascent: Freda Du Faur, Peter Graham, March 1913

routes.name: Du Faur–Cadogan Ridge
routes.description: A straightforward ridge that passes over an attractive unnamed peak (Pt 2352m).
routes.ascent: Franz Malcher, Julius Malcher, E Ranft, February 1914

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: From Graham Saddle, take your pick of gullies and spurs – involving mostly pleasant, steep rock scrambling – to reach the north summit. From there, follow the edge of the snow plateau between De La Beche and the Minarets to the main summit.

routes.name: West Rib
routes.description: An enjoyable rock climb leading directly to the summit. The steep five pitch couloir between the West Ridge and the West Rib has also been climbed. First ascent unknown.

routes.name: De La Beche Ridge
routes.description:
This climb can be interminably long in soft snow conditions, but the lower half can offer a good alternative approach to Graham Saddle.
From De La Beche Corner, ascend the moraine wall onto the lower ridge. The moraine wall is very steep below the old hut site. At least one party has reported a good spot (in 2015) about 400m further up the Tasman, at about BX16 777 747, which leads to the 1560m shelf at BX16 775 749. However, a large collapse from the terrace in November 2017 may have destroyed this. Try your best – everywhere is likely to be sketchy.
From there, head up the ridge to about 1900m, then traverse on the eastern snowslopes and basins up to the plateau between De La Beche and the Minarets, weaving around crevasses as required. Pick a line from the plateau up the final summit block. First ascent unknown.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Dixon Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Previously known as Mt Dixon. The actual Mt Dixon (1556m) is north of the Taramakau River, near Arthur's Pass.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: Gain the ridge either via a steep 150m slope from the Grand Plateau or via the névé between Syme Ridge and Mt Dixon. Then head up a rock buttress and follow the winding arête to the summit. An interesting traverse can be created by descending the South East Ridge (Route 4.66).
routes.ascent: F Gillett, T Newth, A Thompson, A P Thompson, M E Roberts, Dec 1936.

routes.name: The Cave variant
routes.description:
Start up the snowfield approach to the South
Ridge, then head right, aiming for the major
corner/runnel breaching the rock band. Two
pitches of steepening ground lead to a cave.
Climb out and around the roof of the cave on
steep ice and mixed ground (two pitches) to
gain easier climbing to the snowfield, which is
followed to the crest of the South Ridge.

pitches.description: From the Grand Plateau turn the major icecliff on the left and head up. The route usually finishes high on the South Ridge. A somewhat dangerous climb.

routes.name: Direct
routes.description: Takes the main gully through the central rock band, then through the icecliffs above. Finish directly to the summit. Somewhat dangerous.

routes.name: South East Ridge

pitches.description:
This ridge is gained via either (i) the saddle to the north of Pt 2452m then along the narrow ridge, or (ii)
up a steep gully to the right of the large icecliff at the bottom corner of the south-east face. Then follow up
moderate snow slopes to the summit. This is a good descent route from Mt Dixon but takes longer than most
parties anticipate.

routes.ascent: Dan Bryant, Gordon (Snow) Mace, Rod Syme, Jan 1931

routes.name: Give It 80
routes.description:
On right of South East Ridge route (1) . Follow rock-band with left traverses to a
near-vertical 55m ice & rock gully. This crux pitch is committing and
difficult to down-climb, so rest calves midway on rock jutting out on left.
Set belay high to give leader enough rope as it top-outs onto an icy slope
≈30m from ridge. 4 ice-screws for crux (although this was done on 2) and
stakes. Follow ridge to summit on left and descend via South East Ridge route.

pitches.description: From Pioneer Pass, climb up a snow gully onto the Haast-Dixon Ridge.

places.name: West Face
places.description: The névé between Syme Ridge and Mt Dixon provides access to the face. The prominent routes are described, and there are a number of other variations, especially in gullies further left towards Mt Haast.

routes.name: Middle Class White Boys Get Away With Rape

pitches.description: Ill-defined rock rib on left of face
Directly under the summit, ascend from a snow cone to gain a rock rib, which steepens in the middle before some interesting pitches on good rock below the summit.

Ascend a snow couloir and ice gully to the right of the  main buttress and  take the thin left branch, finish up rock to emerge right of the summit. There is no record of who first climbed the R branch.
Ascend easy-angled, sound rock and finish near the top of the South Ridge.
South ridge/west face. 300m of mostly 60 degree ice with some steeper ground. A winter route.
Begins at the base of a lobe of rock beneath the shoulder on the South Ridge. Start up a chimney (crux grade 18), head left onto the face, up an obvious grade 15 rock gully

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Douglas Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description:
The easiest descent route is the West Face of Glacier Pk.
There are a series of gullies on the south side of the Pioneer Ridge, 200m east of Pioneer Hut and adjacent to the Cleves Glacier. When in condition (spring, winter) these gullies provide good short ice climbs. Descend on to the Explorer Névé. First ascents are unknown.

routes.name: East Face
routes.description: Climb scree slopes and a rotten rock ridge onto Emas Dome, then drop onto the Forrest Ross Glacier névé. Climb up under the summit of Douglas and finish by cutting right to the col with Glacier Peak. A more popular alternative when climbing Douglas from the Tasman valley is to traverse Glacier Peak.
routes.ascent: L J Dumbleton, Neville Johnson, J D Willis, December 1935

routes.name: North East (Divide) Ridge

pitches.description: Ascend either Glacier Peak or to the Glacier-Douglas col. Follow the snow ridge to a short 30m ice/rock step to the summit ridge. This is the best way off Douglas and usually involves one abseil. Descend the West Face of Glacier Pk

routes.description: Ascend either Glacier Peak or to the Glacier-Douglas col. Follow the snow ridge to a 30m ice/rock step to the summit ridge. This is the best way off Douglas, and usually involves one 60m abseil. Descend the Glacier Peak West Face route.
routes.ascent: Frank Alack, F Gardiner, T Sheehan, Apr 1931.

routes.name: North Face
routes.description:
Ascend the snow slopes under the West Ridge and up into a narrow couloir to the right of a prominent rock buttress. Where the couloir ends, climb the mixed rock and snow face to the summit.
A collapse from the upper part of Pioneer Ridge, near the summit of Douglas Peak, occurred in Feb 2008. Rocks between 2690 and 3010m fell down the North Face. The rock formed a cone at the base of the slope and a tongue flowed onto the Explorer Glacier. The event occurred during a sequence of warming, possibly as night time temperatures first remained above freezing. Winter ascent 28/8/14 Stepped left at the top of the Couloir and ascended snow slopes to the summit ridge. Variation on new ground.

routes.name: Pioneer Ridge
routes.description: An exhilarating, exposed route which follows an arête, a rock step, another arête, and then leads up to the final rock wall crux. If the top rocks are iced, turn this rock step on the south face. Usually gained from the Explorer Glacier. Described by Newton as ‘certainly the finest climb which I have had in New Zealand, not excepting Mt Cook.’ The first ascent party descended the route; the North East Ridge would be easier to descend, but only if the schrunds on Glacier Peak allow.
routes.ascent: Alex Graham, Henry Newton, Ebenezer Teichelmann, Jan 1907.

pitches.description: An unrelenting ridge between Mt Haidinger and Douglas Peak with many rock towers, varying in soundness. The final rise to the summit of Douglas is probably the hardest section and can be avoided on the east.

places.name: South Face
places.description:
The South face of Douglas looms above the Albert Glacier and its steep arêtes create amphitheatres amidst near-vertical rock. The south face throws out a challenge to any climber who ventures under it. Although the main routes on the face are described below, some variations do exist.
Descent: Until recently, the standard descent was over Glacier Peak. If you plan to go this way check that the west face is not too open with crevasses and a bergschrund, and that you have enough rope and gear for a  abseil off Douglas towards Glacier Peak. People have got ropes stuck on this abseil in the past. Nowadays many people abseil the face on V -threads which puts you back at your skis ...

routes.name: Jefferies- Uren
routes.description: Follows a vague gully on the left side of the face, finishing a little over half way up Pioneer Ridge.

routes.name: Left Hand Gully

pitches.description: Follow the narrow couloir that gradually widens and meets the central arête. Continue up and traverse into the upper Central Couloir and up to the summit. A classic and highly recommended climb.

routes.description: Where it all began—a classic and highly recommended climb. Follow the narrow couloir that gradually widens and meets the central arête. Continue up, traverse right into the upper Central Gully just above the crux in that line, and on to the summit. The Left Hand Gully is quite a bit easier than the Central Gully, being less steep overall. Remember that in 1968 when the first ascent was made, they still climbed ‘in balance,’ using straight picks so that you had to hold the shaft of the axe out from the ice to prevent the pick popping out. Short ropes, pitons, primitive ice protection—an amazing first ascent.

routes.name: Albert Town Direct
routes.description: A creative line that runs up the right-hand front face of the central buttress to the central snow arête and finishes up the upper Left Hand Gully.

routes.name: Interloper
routes.description: A variation to the Central Couloir route that traverses from the right to the left couloir lower  than the original line does, hence missing the central couloir, and  involving four pitches of new ground to reach route 11.58. Dave and Lynn  had decided to put the belay out of the gully on that left wall  and were just missed by large rockfall in the RH Gully so they decided to carry on that line. It was previously named Interceptor in 2003 when climbed by Grant Piper, Paul Scaife, Andrew Haugh, Oct 2003 not realising it had been previously climbed.
routes.ascent: FFA Lynn Bowering & Dave Crow, Nov 1985

routes.name: Denz/Timms

pitches.description: Start up the RH gully then makes a difficult (1971) traverse left to join the Central arete then finishes up the original LH gully finish. This was the FWA of the South Face of Douglas.

routes.description: Follow the lower Right Hand Gully to near the foot of the obvious narrow notch (at two thirds height), and then traverse up and left, below the headwall of the Central Gully, to cross over the central arête, finishing up Route 11.58.

routes.name: Central Gully

pitches.description: Follow the lower right couloir to near the foot of the obvious narrow notch (at 2/3 height), then traverse leftwards into the Central Couloir. Ascend steep ice, for a couple of pitches, which gradually relent, leading to the summit. Superb.

routes.description:
This is one of the great ice climbs of New Zealand—a perfect line on a beautiful face.
Follow Route 11.61 as far as the first section of the leftwards traverse into the Central Gully. Here there are two pitches of steep ice. The first is around 80 degrees and usually forms as water ice. The second pitch gradually relents, and then moderate ground leads to the summit. Abseiling the route has become popular on V threads, which has the added advantage of bringing you back to your skis, but think carefully about whether this is feasible for you on the lower pitches, which can collect a lot of snow. Legend has it that a party, while retreating from just below the crux, dropped both their ropes and had to downclimb the lower pitches.
routes.ascent: Nick Cradock, John Davie, Colin Dodge, Roland Logan, William Trengrove, Aug 1977.

routes.name: Right Hand Gully

pitches.description: Climb the couloir to an obvious deep notch, which can be ascended or else avoided using a ramp on the left. Then exit via a wide couloir onto the Ayres Ridge.

routes.description: Climb the gully to an obvious deep notch, which can be ascended or else avoided using a ramp on the left, and then exit via a wide couloir onto the Ayres Ridge. A good route if you like climbing notches.
routes.ascent: Bill Denz, Ian Ross, Nov 1972. (Denz and Chris Timms climbed up to the base of the notch before continuing on Route 11.61 in Aug 1971)

routes.name: Far Right Rib
routes.description: Follow the rock rib, right of the Right Hand Gully, which joins the Ayres Ridge.

routes.name: Ayres Ridge
routes.description:
An unrelenting ridge between Mt Haidinger and Douglas Peak, with many rock towers varying in soundness. The final rise to the summit of Douglas is probably the hardest section and can be avoided on the east.
In 1977, Dave McNulty described this as the most technically sustained section of the Elie to Harper Saddle traverse, a view affirmed by Phil Penney and Allan Uren during their 1990 winter traverse.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Du Faur Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Main Divide above Hooker Lake, January 2013

routes.name: Hayter Buttress
routes.description: Via the ridge between the Stewart and Hayter Glaciers (separating the two tributaries of Hayter Stream) and then via a rock buttress to the summit.
routes.ascent: Freda Du Faur, Peter Graham, March 1912

routes.name: Cadogan–Madonna Ridge
routes.description: A straightforward, scenic ridge.
routes.ascent: Franz Malcher, Julius Malcher, E Ranft, February 1914

routes.name: North West Ridge
routes.description: From 1540m in the basin below Copland and FitzGerald Passes, sidle onto the lower ridge to begin climbing up vegetated rock slabs (about grade 10). Above 1900m the ridge rises in a series of rock steps (mostly scrambling up to grade 10 with crux grade 13) up to a small peak at 2200m. Abseil from here to a snow notch, and then continue up good rock (grade 10–12) to the blocky summit.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Eagle Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Eagle Peak looks like the head of an eagle scowling along the Main Divide when viewed from high on Mt Thomson’s east face or the upper Donne Glacier.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: Climb via the Main Divide from Maunga Ma.

routes.name: East Face
routes.description: From the Frind-Mueller confluence, ascend part of the way up the true right edge of the lower Frind Glacier, then climb left along rock ledges. Just before reaching the Ngakanohi Glacier turn right to climb up a narrow S-shaped gully that leads to a large, wide rock buttress. Climb the rock (there are several possible options) to gain a vague snow and rock rib to the right of the broad gully that descends from below the summit. Climb the rib directly to the summit.

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: From the Fitzgerald lake, ascend towards the 2416m col until about 1950m, then traverse left beneath bluffs onto the large snowfield below Eagle Peak. In 1953 this snowfield was continuous from Thomson to Eagle Peak, and the first ascent party reported that a rock scramble took them from the head of the snow to the flat summit. It appears that several additional rock steps now exist due to recession of the snow and ice, but a couple of moderate routes to the summit appear feasible.
routes.ascent: D J S Cook, M J Davie, R W Gudgeon, January 1953

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Edith Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: The Strauchon and upper Copland valleys from Tekano Peak, December 2012

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: A steep and rotten ridge from the Hooker valley.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: From Fitzgerald Pass or Copland Pass, traverse around the western side of Lean Peak, ascend snow slopes to the col at Pt 2088m, then up the ridge to the summit. Alternatively (and probably more easily), climb directly from the remnants of the Copland Glacier to Pt 2088m.

routes.name: Requiem for a Dream
routes.description: More than a variation, as the gully is a distinct feature. From the bergschrund at the base of the east face, climb snow and ice gullies 200m left of the main couloir. One pitch going left, then three pitches going right in a series of gullies to reach the ridge.
routes.ascent: Greg Abrahams, Euan Boyd, Steve Farrad, Florian L’Hostis, April 2007

routes.name: Wombats on Heat
routes.description: Ascend a weakness through the rock band below the large snowfield, then up to the Main Divide south of The Footstool. There is a variation that links snowfields to the right of the rock band. This is a good alternative to the Couloir Route if the bergschrund conditions are not favourable. During late summer, snow can be completely absent from this face, and the rock is not worth climbing!

routes.name: Couloir Route
routes.description: From the Tewaewae Glacier ascend the prominent couloir either to the south ridge, or near the summit move right up an offshoot couloir. The bergschrund at the base of the couloir is often troublesome; this route is usually cut off after early summer.

routes.name: Direct
routes.description: Follow the face to the right of the Couloir Route via a shallow gully.

routes.name: Footstolen
routes.description: A short ice route to the right of the Direct, joining the east ridge.

routes.name: Infoleak
routes.description: A short ice route that joins the east ridge.

routes.name: Smash ’n Grab
routes.description: The right-most of three short ice routes, joining the east ridge.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: From Sefton Bivvy ascend the Tewaewae Glacier and cross northwards to gain the ridge where it rises from a level section. Follow the ridge directly to the summit. The rock is a big heap of loosely stacked plates; avoid unless you enjoy self-torment, or it is snow covered.
routes.ascent: Jack Clarke, Peter Graham, Henrik Sillem, March 1906

routes.name: Main Divide
routes.description: A popular route to one of the best viewpoints in the region. From Sefton Bivvy, ascend the Tewaewae Glacier and traverse northwards to cross the East Ridge at the level section, then work up the slopes of the Eugenie Glacier to reach the Main Divide. There are often large crevasses on the Eugenie. Once on the Divide, follow up the north-east snowslopes to the summit. There is often a small step right at the top. This is the regular descent route.

routes.name: From Upper Copland
routes.description: From the snowfield west of Du Faur Peak, connect with snow slopes north-west of Cadogan to reach the col north of the Footstool, and follow the Main Divide route.
routes.ascent: M R Barwell, A F Reid, February 1953

routes.name: Standard Route
routes.description: From the Grand Plateau or upper Haast Ridge, this climb makes for a meditative stroll on which to contemplate the inner workings of the soul.
routes.ascent: Jack Clarke, Peter Graham, Ebenezer Teichelmann, March 1904

routes.name: South East Face
routes.description: Climb scree slopes and a rotten rock ridge onto Emas Dome, then drop onto the Forrest-Ross Glacier névé and find a route up the face through the schrunds.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: Climb scree slopes and a rotten rock ridge onto Emas Dome, then climb up the elegant arête of the east ridge to the summit.

routes.name: East Face
routes.description: Climb scree slopes and a rotten rock ridge onto Emas Dome, and descend north to a small névé between Emas Dome and Frenchay Col. Then climb the wide corridor of snow and ice north of the East Ridge.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: Deceptively good. Rises in a series of rock towers interconnected by snow ridges. A more enjoyable but more time consuming alternative to the West Face, offering a view onto the face for descent purposes. Snow slopes on the left of the crest can provide some useful shortcuts.

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: From the Explorer Névé, (i) ascend the snow face directly to the summit, avoiding icecliffs and bergschrund where necessary. This route is subject to avalanches, particularly in the afternoon. Late in summer, the route can become cut off by crevasses and bergschrund. Alternatively, (ii) the rock rib on the right, below the Glacier-Douglas col, can provide access to the snow slopes. The summit of Glacier Peak and the ridge near the summit can become dangerously corniced. Despite all the warnings, this is a straightforward climb, providing good access to and from Douglas Peak.
routes.ascent: Alex Graham, Henry Newton, Ebenezer Teichelmann, Jan 1907.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Graceful Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Mt Aylmer from above the Murchison Glacier, September 2013

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: From Whymper Saddle, the ridge to the summit is narrow and loose. The base of the ridge could possibly be avoided by traversing either side from the saddle then using a snow lead to regain the ridge. The easiest descent is probably the West Ridge.
routes.ascent: N H Hamilton, M Hamilton, B W Patterson, December 1942

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: A beautiful climb, especially when it comprises snow instead of rock. From the Murchison Névé, gain the col between Mt Aylmer and Graceful, then follow the narrow ridge over a small sub-peak to the summit.

routes.name: Various Routes
routes.description: A short easy ascent from either Governor Col or Pioneer Pass.
routes.ascent: Harold Porter, J Milne, A Ritchie, February 1925

routes.name: Skyline Traverse
routes.description: The south-east and north-west ridges are easily climbed on snow, but care should be taken due to crevasses and exposure down the Whymper side. There are many variations. A traverse of the dome is highly recommended; it helps to scope out the layout of the crevasses on your descent route before setting out.
routes.ascent: Dr Robert von Lendenfeld, Anna von Lendenfeld, H Dew, March 1884

routes.name: Hochstetter Buttress
routes.description: The small buttress on the south face of Hochstetter Dome and visible from Tasman Saddle Hut has also been climbed, and the ice gully next to it. First ascent unknown.

pitches.description:
North Face Grade 4, 1400m
A fantastic setting, a bit of spice, and a distinctly Himalayan feel. Objective hazard due to
icecliffs and the aspect of the face was mimimised on the first ascent by climbing the lower
part in the evening and then finishing the route the next day after a bivvy. From the Whymper
Glacier tend right across a slabby rock face to a gully. Climb this to a shoulder then left back to
the central snowfield and straight up a gully to the headwall (crux). Head left again under the
headwall before going straight up when the terrain allows, to finish in the col between the two
summits of the Dome. Descent to the Tasman Glacier is straightforward.

An appropriate first short tour is to Hochstetter Dome. From either hut climb to Aylmer Saddle (between the peaks of Hochstetter and Aylmer) and carry skis along the ridge to Hochstetter’s High Peak (2827m). Alternatively ascend on skis by traversing under the high peak and approaching the Low Peak (2810m) from the west. A good long ski descent is from Low Peak via the broad western shoulder towards Lendenfeld saddle and then south-west towards the floor of the Tasman Glacier. 4-6 hours return to the hut.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: Ascend to Baker Saddle, then follow the snow arête until it runs out below icecliffs. Climb the rock buttresses to the left of the cliffs on sound rock or early in the summer follow an ice gully. Then follow the winding arête to the summit. This used to be a dangerous route due to the frequently active icecliffs, but this seems to be less of an issue these days –perhaps there are some advantages to retreating glaciers!

routes.name: East Face Direct
routes.description:
The most elegant route is up a rounded rib that drops from the summit to the Hooker. From the upper Hooker Glacier, climb snow fields and rock ribs, keeping an eye out for ice avalanches from cliffs to the right and left. Beware of soft snow slides later in the day in summer.
Adam Darragh and Parish Robbins climbed a ‘Baker Saddle East Face’ variant in the summer of 1997.
routes.ascent: Hans Leitner, Eberhard von Terzi, January 1962

routes.name: To L & LP Col
routes.description:
A route begins under Mt Jellicoe and traverses up under Mt Low to gain the col to the right of the summit of La Perouse.
J Keys and Noel Sissons climbed a variant using a rib on the East Face in December 1971.
routes.ascent: Gordon Hasell, Fred Page, Richard Seddon, Richard Tornquist, January 1958

routes.name: Main Divide
routes.description: From the summit of Mt Jellicoe, either traverse Mt Low and the ridge to La Perouse or skirt below the ridge on the western slopes and up to the summit. This is a long climb but still the most common descent route. Route finding can be tricky if descending this route after climbing a different route – take care.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description:
A wonderful climb. It’s a long way from the valley floor, and most parties have found it best to climb from a higher camp or bivvy. From the large grassy flat at 1050m, ascend scrub and tussock slopes towards the location of the rock bivvy marked on the topomap. This is actually the centre of a scattered collection of boulders, only some of which provide good shelter. A good bivvy rock near BX15 623 695 at about 1520m has been used by several parties. Others have reported good rocks to the right of the large prominent snow gully at about 1650m (100m below the main ridge), with a pool of water nearby.
From the rock bivvies, either:
(i) gain the ridge, and then traverse over several rotten rock steps near Pt 2130m. Then ascend a steep snow face onto the upper arête and follow this up onto the spacious summit area; or alternatively
(ii) several parties have bypassed the rock steps by heading east from the rock bivvies and climbing snow slopes to the north of the lower ridge, joining the normal route around 2400m.
routes.ascent: Alec Graham, Robert Low, Henry Newton, Ebenezer Teichelmann, February 1906

routes.name: Gulch Route
routes.description: A stunning, but very dangerous climb. From the head of the narrow Gulch Glacier (beware of avalanches off the huge slabs near the West Ridge) follow snow leads tending right towards the base of the obvious rock step on the south-west ridge, and then tend left on snowfields to circumvent the rock step. Continue up the south ridge to the summit. Access from the Gulch to the south-west ridge is likely to be cut off in late summer.

routes.name: South West Ridge
routes.description: A rarely climbed route in a stunning position. From the Strauchon Glacier, ascend the Cuttance Col route to gain the crest of the Navigator Range, and then follow the ridge eastwards past Pt 2356m. When the obvious rock step in the ridge is reached (the top of the Slab Route, route 14.20), cut onto the Gulch Face and ascend directly on snow to where the south ridge meets the south-west ridge. Continue up the snow arête to the summit. The simplest way to descend is probably to retrace your steps back to the Strauchon.
routes.ascent: Tom Barcham, Ash Cunningham, Alec Witten-Hannah, January 1953

routes.name: Slab Route
routes.description: Climb the diagonal slab that runs up the entire face (crux). The upper portion of the slab is usually snow covered and there may be a small icecliff to negotiate. Continue up the south-west ridge, bypassing the obvious rock step, to reach the summit.

routes.name: Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure
routes.description:
An enigmatic route, the lower portion of which can’t be seen until you’ve done most of the approach over Baker Saddle. Awaiting a second, or better yet, a direct, ascent. Access to the base of the route is threatened by icecliffs on both sides of the south ridge. Start up the obvious main ice line that drips down the face.
Avoid the steepest 3–4 pitches at mid-height by heading up a prominent ramp which angles towards the south ridge, then traverse back into the line below the uppermost cliffs. Finish either side of the icecliff above to join the upper south ridge, and then follow this to the summit. The first ascent was completed in 14 pitches of generally WI3 to WI4 ice.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Lean Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Main Divide above Hooker Lake, January 2013

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: A short ascent up steepish rock from Copland Pass.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: Gain the west ridge up snow gullies from the basin below Copland Pass and follow the ridge to the summit. Snow leads out to the right lead through the final steeper section to the summit.

routes.name: South Face

pitches.description: From the névé between Syme Ridge and Mt Dixon climb directly to the summit detouring where icecliffs dictate. Formerly referred to at the East Face. Has been skied.

routes.ascent: Rob Rainsbury, Dick Strong, Keith Thompson, John Visser, Dec 1970.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description:
From Marcel Col, the route is straightforward on moderate snow slopes, although hard ice can form easily here, especially in winter. You’ll also find good evidence of climate change here: a large gap is starting to form about halfway up the ridge and soon we may see exposed rock, which will make this route more difficult. A sad sign of the times.
This is the most common way to access Engineer Col and the North Shoulder of Tasman. It’s also the recommended descent route, but beware of the cornice that sometimes forms on the summit of Lendenfeld.

pitches.description: Gain the large snow shelf left of Hamilton-Berry Rib by a short rock/mixed step. Ascend to the top left end of the snow shelf through a mixed gully to the summit ice cap.

routes.name: North Gully
routes.description: Follow the chimney immediately left of Hamilton-Berry Rib, or mixed ground either side of the gully. Six rope lengths to the snowfield.

routes.name: Hamilton-Berry Rib
routes.description: The bottom 200m provides steep, sound climbing up to grade 14. The rib then slowly relents to form a ‘Giant’s Staircase’. A good, classic route.

routes.name: Midsummer Muntaneering
routes.description:
Probable new route between Hamilton Berry rib and NW rib.
This rock route takes the right hand visual profile as seen from Pioneer Hut.
Start up snow just left of bottom of rib and cut onto rock at any convenience. Follow the rib traversing along pinnacles, chevals, loose sections, until the obvious black triangular wall is attained.
Then traverse a rising ledge/ramp up the black wall from left to right. Finish straight up wide cracks or shallow chimney (crux 15). The route then merges with the upper section of the Hamilton Berry rib.
This is a challenging and interesting mountaineering route which requires some care, however it is not technical rock climb.

routes.name: North West Couloir

pitches.description: Up the snow and ice gully between the two rock buttresses. This route may lack ice later in summer.

routes.description: Up the snow and ice gully between the two rock buttresses. This route may lack snow/ice later in summer, making rockfall almost constant.
routes.ascent: Merv English, Peter Hillary, Nena Ritchie, Jul 1978.

pitches.description: Parallels the Hamilton-Berry Rib, with good climbing on slabs and ribs of excellent rock.

routes.name: Adventure Philosophy
routes.description: Start up the gully on the left-hand side of the face until a ramp system is reached. Follow the ramp right until near the middle, then climb straight up to the summit. A few grade 13-14 pitches.

routes.name: The Mutant
routes.description:
This is the striking five pitch chimney in the middle of the face. In summer this is a great rock climb on a sunny face; in winter and spring it provides classic mixed and ice climbing with good rock protection. The second ascent team used a small amount of aid on the crux pitch, due to melting ice. From the top of the chimney, five more pitches take you to the summit. 9 pitches.
Has not had a winter ascent.
routes.ascent: F.A John McCartney, Andy McFarlane, summer 1995

routes.name: The Fiend

pitches.description: Follow easy ground weaving up to a roof/overhanging flake, place gear under the roof and follow the flake around and up-build belay here.

Climb right off the belay #5/6 cam useful here or climb 5m lay back off-width in unprotected to good pro, follow the crack up and right till you reach the slab and build a belay on the left (used a horn and a few cams)
Work your way up and left follow the natural flow of the climb and belay on a horn and nut or go to ledge and build a belay easy ground takes you to the summit from here.

routes.description: Start 10m right of The Mutant. Starts on less solid rock but the rock becomes very good where you need it to be. The second and third pitches are on bomber granite-like rock with sandpaper texture which climbs just as good as it looks.
routes.ascent: FFA Justin Wimmer and Michael Lehmann 30 Sept 2024

routes.name: West Face Direct
routes.description: A hard climb on excellent rock (sustained grade 15-16), commencing to the right of The Mutant chimney. ‘Similar to, but harder than the South Face of Hicks’ – Ken Hyslop.
routes.ascent: Lindsay Bell, Don Bogie and Ken Hyslop

routes.name: Allen-Williams
routes.description: Head up the gully to the right of the West Face Direct route until you can access a line that leads to a ledge system through the prominent arête. Once on the face proper, continue up two more pitches to join the Direct.

routes.name: South West Ridge

pitches.description: This ridge is usually used when traversing Lendenfeld en route to Tasman. Between the summit and the col the ridge is straightforward. Glacier access can sometimes become cut off.

routes.description: This ridge is usually used when traversing Lendenfeld en route to Tasman. Between the summit and the col the ridge is straightforward. Glacier access can sometimes become cut off.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Madonna
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Main Divide above Hooker Lake, January 2013

routes.name: Standard Route
routes.description: Find a way up onto the moraine terrace where Hooker Hut used to sit, then scramble up the enjoyable ridge to the summit. Exposed, broken rock in places, but not too steep.
routes.ascent: Jack Clarke, J E Walker, Hugh Wright, January 1911

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: A straightforward scramble from FitzGerald Pass or Copland Pass.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Malaspina
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: A prominent gully north of Malaspina may provide a quick alternative to the route to the Grand Plateau over Clarke Saddle.  See Clarke Saddle and the "Via Clarke Saddle" Route of Mt Teichelmann/Rakirua.

routes.name: East Spur
routes.description: From the Linda Glacier opposite Teichelmann’s Corner a broad snow shoulder leads up to just below the summit of Malaspina.

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: This route leads to a prominent point between Vancouver and the mapped summit of Mt Malaspina (to be fair, the actual position of Malaspina is a little vague). Ascend a rock ridge onto a major bump in the ridge. Then across a sweeping snow saddle to a final buttress of four rope lengths which lead to the summit.
routes.ascent: David Elphick, Mike White, February 1957 (lower section)

routes.name: South East Face
routes.description: Direct from the Mueller Glacier to the Ngakanohi Glacier and continue up the East Rib to the summit. Glacial retreat since the first ascent has made the lower part of this climb loose, unpleasant, and quite dangerous. This route will only get worse with increased glacial retreat. It’s included here more from a historical view point. Not recommended.

routes.name: Ngakanohi Glacier Route
routes.description: From the Frind-Mueller confluence, ascend part way up the true right edge of the lower Frind Glacier, then climb left along rock ledges to gain the base of the Ngakanohi (‘the eyes’) Glacier above Ngaroimata (‘the tears’) Falls. Traverse diagonally up to the top of the glacier to join the East Rib of Maunga Ma, which is followed direct to the summit up rotten rock (covered by snow early in the season).
routes.ascent: Otto Frind, Conrad Kain, Peter Graham, February 1914

routes.name: North Ridge
routes.description: From the Fitzgerald lake, climb to the 2416m col then follow the ridge to the summit. The route of the first full ascent from the west.
routes.ascent: D J S Cook, M J Davie, R W Gudgeon, T P D Thompson, January 1953

routes.name: West Face
routes.description:
From the Fitzgerald lake, climb towards Twain Col then climb moderate snow slopes up a blunt ridge direct to the summit.
Christopher Johnson and Archie Scott also technically made the first ascent of Maunga Ma from the west. After climbing over Maunga Ma from the Hermitage, their party descended 400m on the west side for the night, and then Johnson and Scott climbed back to the summit to collect a cache of gear before descending to Harpers Rock.
routes.ascent: Christopher Johnson, Graham Riley, Archie Scott (descended), December 1935

routes.name: Vervoorn Vamoose
routes.description: A descending route from Maunga Ma to the Fitzgerald Flats via a diagonal shingle bench below Awatea has been used when the descent from Maunga Ma to the Mueller was obscured by inclement weather. This is technically straightforward, but it could be difficult to stay on route.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: Meteor Pk
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: Main Divide peaks above the Franz Josef névé, December 2011

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: Has some surprisingly tricky steps en route to the summit.

routes.name: North West Face
routes.description: This is a popular playground for instruction groups – there are several possibilities.

routes.name: South West Ridge
routes.description: Easy apart from the final step to the summit, which involves steepish climbing on rotten rock.

https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.name: The Minarets
https://climbnz.org.nz/nz/si/aoraki-tai-.description: The Minarets comprise two peaks, west (3031m) and east (3040m).

routes.name: Original (Standard) Route
routes.description: A short snow climb from the plateau between Mt De La Beche and The Minarets. The plateau is reached from the Haupapa Tasman Glacier via the West Ridge or De La Beche Ridge, and from the Kā Roimata o Hine Hukatere Franz Joseph Glacier via the Minaret’s West Face. The technical grade is from the plateau.

routes.name: Ranfurly Glacier
routes.description: From the Tasman Glacier there are a number of variations ascending the glacier. This route is highly dependent on favourable crevasse conditions.
routes.ascent: Freda Du Faur, Laurence Earle, Peter Graham, B Spencer, January 1910

routes.name: North East Ridge
routes.description: A long climb, usually approached along the Main Divide via Mt Coronet, Mt Meeson, Mt Vic and Mt Gold Smith. The ridge crest can be followed except for one or two places where a traverse on the west is necessary.
routes.ascent: Harry Ayres, Mick Bowie, F F Simmons, January 1938

routes.name: North West Face
routes.description: From the Geikie Glacier, traverse around onto one of the feeder arms of the Spencer Glacier and ascend the prominent rock face onto the West Minaret via a series of interconnecting snow ramps that start at the centre of the face (400m of mixed climbing). The ramps steepen towards the top and finish three to four easy rope lengths west of the summit.

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: From north of Graham Saddle, ascend the prominent snow slopes to the saddle between De La Beche and the Minarets. There can be large schrunds at any time of year on this face, which involves sustained 40-degree snow slopes. The rock spurs nearer De La Beche have also been used. It’s also possible to traverse the steep slopes under De La Beche and above the Rudolph Glacier, arriving high on the De La Beche Ridge.

routes.name: Main Divide Routes
routes.description: An easy ascent from Graham Saddle or the saddle between Moonlight and Rudolf.

routes.name: Original Route
routes.description: A simple climb from the Main Divide or from the Franz Josef névé. Straight up the middle of the face provides some good practice on moderately steep snow (five pitches).

routes.name: Egg Memorial Route
routes.description: A good rock route when there is not much snow around – quite often these days! Climbs the prominent arête/buttress feature about 300m west of Aigrette from the névé to the summit (Pt MUMC, about 2560m). Eight pitches on mostly very good rock, with some rubbly ledges. Start wherever you think is best to ensure your line includes the beautiful slab of pitch two. Highly recommended by the first ascentionists, who descended by abseiling to the left of the route.
routes.ascent: Luke Gogolkiewicz, Stuart Hollaway, Nathan Jancauskas, Gaetan Riou, January 2012

routes.name: South East Rib
